newsitem.title: GERMANY: SWIMMING-TOP CONTENDER KARLSSON PULLS OUT OF EURO CHAMPIONSHIPS.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-TOP CONTENDER KARLSSON PULLS OUT OF EURO CHAMPIONSHIPS.

text.p: Sweden's Louise Karlsson, a multi-gold medallist, has pulled out of the European sprints and short-course swimming championships because of a bad cold, organisers said on Thursday.
Karlsson won eight gold medals, including four in the 100 metres individual medley, at the European sprint championships between 1991 and 1994.

No swimmer, apart from Germany's Sandra Voelker who won 12 sprint golds, has collected so many titles at the sprint meeting, which has been incorporated into these new European short-course championships.
Karlsson, holder of the world-best 100 individual medley time, also gained a 200 individual medley bronze at the 1995 world short-course championships in Rio de Janeiro.
The championships, already without all Europe's Atlanta Olympic champions, have been further depleted by the withdrawal of German freestyler Kerstin Kielgass after an appendix operation.
Kielgass, 200 freestyle bronze medallist at the 1992 Barcelona Olympics, finished fourth in both the 400 and 800 freestyle at the Atlanta Games.
Kielgass, reigning European long-course 200 freestyle champion, underwent the operation last Friday, three days after her 27th birthday.

Her absence cut the women's 800 freestyle entry list to just five swimmers, reducing the event to a final on Friday and leaving just one series of heats for Thursday evening's championship prelude -- the men's 400 freestyle.
The meeting, bringing together 248 swimmers from 30 countries, gets properly underway on Friday. There are 38 finals, six more than in the Olympic swimming programme.
Prize money is on offer for the first time, with 5,000 marks ($3,200) the reward for a European record.

Harm Beyer, general secretary of European swimming's governing body (LEN), said the sportswear company sponsoring the meeting would provide the money for the first two records and LEN would pay for any others.
Beyer, who anticipates half a dozen European records will fall in Rostock, said e LEN had insured itself against big pay-outs with a London broker.

Voelker, who gained silver in the 100 freestyle and bronze in the 50 freestyle at the Atlanta Olympics, won the 50 freestyle twice and the 50 backstroke four times at the European sprint championships, last held in Stavanger, Norway, in 1994.
She is the top competitor at this meeting, racing in the 50 and 100 freestyle, 50 and 100 butterfly and 50 backstroke, plus relays.
Voelker said her aim was to retain her 50 backstroke and 50 freestyle titles: "I'll let everything else just happen."
Alexander Popov, stabbed in a Moscow street in August a month after retaining his Olympic 50 and 100 freestyle titles, is the most prominent absentee.

Fellow Russian Denis Pankratov, Ireland's Michelle Smith and Belgium's Frederik Deburghgraeve are among other Atlanta gold medallists who have passed up the meeting in a crowded international calendar.
